intention: Module boundaries match the data: analytics owns what the app calculates, charging owns charge data, telemetry owns only what Tesla reported, and an app layer owns ProcessVehicleData.
request: MAG-26 — modular monolith refactoring: give the platform an analytics module, a charging module, and an application layer, so no module stores another's derived values.

decisions.decision: Did not start T6 despite autopilot ON and budget clear.
decisions.why: T6 drops columns holding real data and adds a table - the database design gate needs the owner, and Step 2's interview cannot run while they sleep. Guessing risks data loss.

decisions.decision: SUPERSEDES D2's table move. The run log STAYS in telemetry as poll_attempts, gaining run_id + triggered_by; app passes both DOWN as parameters. process_runs is not created and internal/app gets no schema.
decisions.why: D2 justified the move with 'triggered_by is not something Tesla reported', but that purity test belongs to vehicle_snapshots. poll_attempts always held our own facts (attempted_at, outcome, reason), so triggered_by is not foreign to it.

decisions.decision: Grain stays one row per (vehicle, run); run_id correlates one invocation, per-run facts come from GROUP BY run_id.
decisions.why: Preserves telemetry D5's per-vehicle sleep signal and suits the read-heavy profile. It also makes the table a POLL log, which is the reason it belongs where its writer lives (RD2).

decisions.decision: ProcessVehicleData has THREE named steps - sync fleet, process charging, recalculate analytics - and Scheduler + API are peer driving adapters that CALL it, never inside it.
decisions.why: Owner's own diagram. D2 said 'sync + recalculate'; the charging mirror T6 shipped is a first-class step, not part of sync.

decisions.decision: Scheduler moves telemetry -> cmd/poller, not into app. app exposes only the use case. Owner accepts that cmd/poller has no tests.
decisions.why: Scheduler and the future API are both driving adapters, so both sit outside app. Cost: nextRun math loses its test coverage and --once stays the only wiring check.

decisions.decision: CollectAll widens to CollectAll(ctx, RunContext{RunID, TriggeredBy}); telemetry owns the TriggeredBy type and its constants. The mirror mapping moves cmd/poller -> app wholesale, as T6 D7 already planned; charging keeps its MUST NOT import telemetry rule.
decisions.why: Typed constants beat a bare string. On the mapping: analytics is a derived read model so mapping is its domain, but charging owns primary data - the 11-field map is a propagation policy, which is app's.

decisions.decision: DATABASE DESIGN GATE CONFIRMED. ALTER TABLE poll_attempts ADD COLUMN run_id UUID, ADD COLUMN triggered_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduler'. No CHECK, no index, run_id nullable, --once records 'scheduler'.
decisions.why: Owner asked for the cheapest form and does not need --once distinguishable. NOT NULL DEFAULT backfills in one metadata-only statement; the Go typed constant already guards values; no reader means no index yet (T6 I6).

decisions.decision: SUPERSEDES RD5. Scheduler moves telemetry -> internal/app, NOT cmd/poller. Its 4 Scheduler tests move with it. cmd/poller keeps wiring only.
decisions.why: RD5 would put 131 lines of timer/date logic into cmd/, against CLAUDE.md's 'cmd/ stays thin (zero business logic)' - and T7 exists to REMOVE logic from that file. Symmetry with a parked, undesigned T8 API is taste; the rule is written.

decisions.decision: Dispatched the RD8 artifacts amendment on Opus rather than the default Sonnet.
decisions.why: It rewrites the binding decision four implementation waves are built on, and inverts a claim (coverage loss) threaded through design, tasks and AGENTS.md. A missed thread ships a false rationale.

T7 interview COMPLETE (RD2-RD6). The owner spotted an asymmetry worth recording even though they chose not to fix it now: cmd/poller holds ONLY orchestration for the analytics step (deriveVehicleMetrics lives inside analytics) but orchestration PLUS an 11-field mapping for the charging step, because charging is forbidden to import telemetry while analytics is not. Two rules for the same situation. Moving the mapping to app carries that asymmetry forward; the owner accepted it on the reasoning that a derived read model mapping from siblings is intrinsic, whereas populating a primary-data module from another's table is application policy.
